picks.title: Advancing science & engineering with Antigravity's /teamwork
picks.rationale: Primary-source release: Google's /teamwork runs parallel Gemini agents with automated verifiers and delivers a fully Lean 4-formalized proof of the Courtade-Kumar conjecture plus a machine-checked Weil conjectures formalization.
picks.excerpt: Google's multi-agent /teamwork pairs researchers with parallel Gemini agents plus automated verifiers; results include a full Lean 4-formalized proof of the 2013 Courtade-Kumar information-theory conjecture and a machine-checked Weil conjectures formalization.

picks.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
picks.rationale: UCSB-led Neuron proof-of-concept: a deep-learning model designs cortical stimulation patterns that better control the phosphene shapes a blind volunteer perceives — AI as a neuroscience method, not a clinical product (not in the medicine pool, no cross-section clash).
picks.excerpt: UC Santa Barbara and partners used a deep learning system to design electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes in a blind volunteer's visual cortex, improving control and prediction of perceived phosphene shapes (Neuron proof-of-concept).

picks.title: AI improves cosmic particle scans to locate hidden objects more accurately in simulations
picks.rationale: Tartu/GScan ML on straight and scattered cosmic-ray muons cuts wrongly merged objects in muon tomography from about 15% to 2% in simulation — a quantified gain in a physics imaging method (IEEE Access).
picks.excerpt: University of Tartu and GScan trained ML models on both straight-through and scattered cosmic-ray muons for muon tomography; in simulations a hybrid method located hidden objects better and cut wrongly merged nearby objects from about 15% to 2% (IEEE Access).

picks.title: This AI finds patterns in visual brain activity and turns them into pictures
picks.rationale: Brain-IT reconstructs seen images from fMRI and runs the reverse mapping — a distinct model and paper from the 11-14 Concept2Brain (EEG simulation) card, adding the cognitive-science lane.
picks.excerpt: A new AI model, Brain-IT, reconstructs images from fMRI brain scans and runs the reverse, predicting what an image would look like as visual-cortex activity.

picks.title: Finding romance with AI: Study explores benefits, limits of chatbot intimacy
picks.rationale: University of Michigan survey of 463 adults compares chatbot, long-distance and in-person relationships: similar intimacy ratings, but chatbot emotional intimacy tracks with loneliness — a new psychology result, separate from the 11-05 companion-update study.
picks.excerpt: University of Michigan survey of 463 U.S. adults in chatbot, long-distance and in-person relationships finds similar emotional and intellectual intimacy ratings, but in chatbot relationships emotional intimacy tracked with more loneliness unless social support was accounted for (Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans).

dedup.note: Dropped as duplicates: ScienceDaily 'Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images' (likely-repeat of the 11-06 Universe Today JWST digital-twin card, same study); SingularityHub AutoDNA 'AI Agents Ran a Biology Lab' (same Nature AutoDNA story published 11-07). Cross-section: none of the picks appear in published_urls.json for any section, and the bionic-eye story is absent from today's medicine pool. Brain-IT (fMRI image reconstruction) is a different model/paper from the 11-14 Concept2Brain EEG card, so kept as new. Antigravity /teamwork is a new feature release, distinct from the 11-04 Antigravity cheminformatics post. Not picked on judgement: Phys.org bacLIFE plant-pathogen genes (pathogen-gene content carries classifier risk; related to 10-29 rice card); Phys.org Euclid lenses (ML only the first filter stage, AI incidental); Tech Xplore PI-GAE aerodynamics and CLARA bioreactor (lower novelty; keep Tech Xplore at 1); GEN protein-design feature (survey); Medical Xpress SfN roundup (preview); Live Science birdsong (Q&A, no new paper). Outlets: 5 distinct, 1 each.
